note: Every trader the campaign stands in a town. A trader is an entity, and a re-export regenerates every region and entity file from the WorldPainter project, so a trader summoned in game is erased by every export. This manifest is the source: tools/traders.py function writes the re-application function, and the post-export procedure in docs/world-building/REEXPORT.md (R14) runs it. Nothing is summoned by hand. tools/validate_data.py checks the static rules, and exactly-one presence in a stopped world passed with --world-save.

fields.id: stable id; the entity carries the tags cobblers_vendor and cobblers_vendor_<id>
fields.settlement: the town in data/placements.json whose plaza, or building, the trader stands in
fields.template: the installed shopkeeper template the trader's entity is read from (its trade list, name and look)
fields.source: where that template ships, and its licence: placed by resource id, never copied into the repo
fields.position: {x, y, z}: the block the trader stands in: one above the plaza paving the town plan grades, or, for a trader in a building, one above the floor of its template's shopkeeper jigsaw
fields.status: planned (not in the campaign world), placed (re-applied by the function), verified (checked in game)
fields.chosen_because: why this trader, in this town
fields.stock: regional (sells what the stock policy leaves), withdrawn (the policy leaves nothing, so the trader is not summoned and any copy standing is removed) or mart (sells exactly the policy's Mart items); tools/traders.py refuses to write a function if this disagrees with the policy; stones (the Exchange: sells exactly stock_policy.stones's items, an authored shop that replaces the template's, and buys nothing)
fields.building: optional: the placed building (a tools/place_town.py building id) the trader stands in; its position is that template's shopkeeper jigsaw carried through the placement
fields.facing: optional: which way a NoAI trader looks (south, west, north, east): a Mart clerk faces its door

stock_policy.status: interim, 2026-09-21: until the badge-gated stock plan replaces it. That plan is now docs/mechanics/MARKET_GATING.md (the mechanism: per-player dialogue-option visibility on a cobblers:flag/<id> probe) with the shelf town by town in docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md section 1. The gated counters are now data/markets.json (tools/markets.py, pack cobblers_markets, keepers by reapply R17M, 2026-10-03): a keeper beside each Mart releases the withheld lines item by item at a badge, so the blanket withholding below is now the CLERK's floor, not the region's. Not run in game. The one thing added ahead of that plan is stock_policy.trainer_card, because the card is a prerequisite for meeting any trainer at all, not a rung on the shelf (PROGRESSION_LADDER section 5.1)
stock_policy.why: The shopkeeper templates came stocked by BCA for a generic world: ultra balls, max revives, full restores and X items on a plaza in the first town. Until stock is gated by badges, a trader sells only what its town produces: seeds, herbs, mulch, fish, game, food. Anything that wins a battle or catches a Pokemon is withheld.
stock_policy.withhold_items_why: the herbs that are cheap battle medicine or a held item: a revival herb is a revive for 400 against the Mart's 2,000, energy root and heal powder are a hyper potion and a full heal, big root is a held item

mart.name: Poké Mart
mart.status: owner decision 2026-09-25: basic stock in every town from the start; badge-gated stock comes later
mart.why: A town with no balls is not a town. Every Mart sells Poké Balls, Potions and Antidotes from the first visit, at the general shopkeeper's prices (200, 200, 100); what wins battles stays withheld until the badge-gated stock replaces this policy.
mart.tiers_status: built as data 2026-10-06 (the owner's play-test note 9: 'The Poke Mart (Cobblemon's default) never sells more than the default few items: scale it with gyms'). Generated by tools/traders.py (mart_tier, mart_shop_items); NOT run in game
mart.tiers_why: A Mart clerk at tier N keeps, from its own shopkeeper template (bca:stores/store_workers/shopkeeper_ds_general, which already stocks every one of these at its own price: read from the 2026-10-05 snapshot's COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31.zip), the basic items plus every tier line with badges <= N. Nothing is authored: the shop is the template's, filtered wider, so the prices are the template's (great 600, ultra 800, super 700, hyper 1,500, revive 2,000, max potion 2,500, full heal 400) and no new offer shape is introduced. The seven items the counters also sell (data/markets.json: super potion at gym 2's town, great ball 3, full heal 4, ultra ball 6, max potion 7, full restore and max revive 8) enter the Mart at the counter's own badge, so the counter is the first to carry a thing and the Mart catches up in the NEXT town on the road; a Mart never sells what its own town's counter sells (tests/test_mart_tiers.py). The other lines follow the main series' badge-count Marts (status heals early, revive mid, the max lines late). Tier 8 has no Mart today: full restore and max revive stay at Holdfast's counter, and are listed for a League Mart if one is built
mart.tier_rule: a Mart clerk's tier is the number of badges a critical-path player holds ARRIVING at its town, i.e. the gym the town follows: hometown and gym 1's town 0, gym N's town N-1 (data/towns.json order). An off-path Mart takes the tier of the critical-path town whose centre (data/towns.json) is nearest the clerk's own position (straight line; the clerk's position, because towns.json still puts Pacifidlog at its pre-move site, REVIEW 58): Steepside (tea_town) 0 by Stoneford, Northlight 5 by Tilpey Cross, the Mining Town 6 by Cinderlee, Pacifidlog 7 and Sunset West 7 by Holdfast. A record may carry mart_tier with mart_tier_why to override. WHY BY TOWN, NOT BY PLAYER: since 2026-10-06 every seller is a CobbleDollars merchant with the shop screen (data/markets.json decision counters_are_merchants), which shows one list to every player and cannot gate a line per player (docs/mechanics/MARKET_GATING.md section 1), so the Marts tier by the town's position on the route, the way the counters now do. A player who reaches a town early buys its shelf early; that is the cost the owner accepted for the counters
mart.tier_rule_caveats: Sunset West is 987 from Holdfast but 1,694 from Pallet on foot, so a player can walk there with no badges and buy tier-7 stock (ultra balls, max potion); Pacifidlog is reached by ferry. Pacifidlog's deck is 1,748 from Holdfast and reached by sea. Both are 'don't limit the player' (the owner, 2026-10-05) unless the owner sets mart_tier on the record

early_reach_pricing.status: built as data 2026-10-07 (reviews N67, N93); the convenience band added 2026-10-08 (the owner's answer 3 to the Wave A report). Generated by tools/traders.py (early_reach_prices, applied in apply_stock_policy and training_shop); NOT run in game
early_reach_pricing.decision: the owner, 2026-10-07: an early-reachable town may SELL late-game stock, but its prices must be out of reach early. A counter or Mart cannot gate a line per player (data/markets.json decision counters_are_merchants), so the price is the gate. The owner, 2026-10-08: 'no. 9,500 is half a Master Ball for a tier-1 heal. Re-price so it is a convenience' -- the gate is for LATE stock; a low tier is a premium, not a wall
early_reach_pricing.criterion: a tier line (stock_policy.mart.tiers or stock_policy.mart.training.tiers, badges T) sold at a clerk listed here, whose town is reachable with R badges, falls in one of three bands by its distance d = T - R. d <= 0: the normal price (the template's for a Mart line, the authored price for a training line). 1 <= d <= convenience_within: the CONVENIENCE band, the normal price times convenience_markup, rounded UP to round_to. d > convenience_within: the INCOME GATE, a price MORE than the most money the income model lets a player with fewer than T badges have: a player holding b badges earns leg b+1 while holding them, so the most a player with T-1 badges has is cumulative_by_badge[T] (data/markets.json income_basis: the income through T badges, before any spending), and the price is the smallest multiple of round_to strictly above that. No band ever prices a line below its normal price. The basics keep the template's price
early_reach_pricing.convenience_within_why: a line within two badges of the town's reach is one the player meets at its normal price within the next two gym towns on the road: buying it early saves a walk, not a gym. At reach 0 the band is exactly tiers 1-2 -- the four status cures, the super potion, and the training kit's selector (power items) and undo (fresh-start mochi, EV-lowering berries) -- none of which changes what a player can catch or survive, because the Pokemon Center heals for nothing between fights. Tier 3 is the first line that does (the great ball, which data/markets.json introduces at gym 3's counter), so the income gate starts there. Owner-adjustable: one number
early_reach_pricing.convenience_markup_why: twice the normal price is a premium a player notices and can pay out of the first leg: at reach 0 the dearest convenience line is the power item at 3,000, a third of the badge-1 leg (9,475, RELAYED). At 2x the super potion (1,400) is worse value per hit point than the potions it replaces (the 200 basic), so it sells the convenience of one action in battle, not more healing per dollar. Owner-adjustable: one number
early_reach_pricing.income_is: RELAYED, not measured (income_basis.relayed true: PROGRESSION_LADDER.md model B at cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier 1.25). A player who earns faster than the model (grinding, or the base bank's AFK food buys, review N64) can buy earlier: the price gate is only as good as the income model

sunset_west_mart.why: data/towns.json sunset_west: gates [], access 'on foot along the southern coast, or by sea; not locked'. tools/economy_audit.py measures its clerk 1,711 blocks from the 0-badge critical route; nothing between needs a badge. Its tier is 7 by Holdfast (tier_rule)

sea_town_mart.why: the owner, 2026-10-08 (answer 2 to the Wave A report): 'it has no working ferry, so arriving at 0 badges means arriving somewhere unusable' -- Pacifidlog is priced for the designed visit, an optional detour between badge 6 and badge 8 (LONG_ISLE.md section 2). data/towns.json sea_town still says gates [] and 'by water only ... not locked', so a 0-badge sailor who does arrive buys tiers 1-6 at their normal prices (ultra balls at the template's 800): the owner's accepted cost. Its tier is 7 by Holdfast (tier_rule), so only the tier-7 line (max potion) is above reach, in the convenience band

trainer_card.status: built as data 2026-10-01 (the owner: make rctmod:trainer_card obtainable). One authored category appended to one Mart clerk's filtered shop (tools/traders.py card_shop), in the offer shape the shopkeeper templates themselves carry. That it sells in game is NOT RUN: the same gap as the Exchange's proof P-7. The gated dialogue counters of MARKET_GATING.md are not built and this is not one of them
trainer_card.what_it_fixes: modpack/config/rctmod-server.toml:87 sets spawningRequiresTrainerCard = true: a player with no card in inventory meets no naturally spawned RCT trainer, and RCT's trainer-association NPC has nothing to offer. Measured on a throwaway staging world 2026-10-01: our clerk's live shop was exactly three categories (poke_ball 200, potion 200, antidote 100) and the string trainer_card appeared 0 times in the whole cobblers_vendors pack, so the card was unobtainable anywhere in the region. It is NOT the campaign: that config key's own comment says it does not affect trainer spawners, and every authored fight reaches a player through a spawner or summon_persistent (the eight leaders, the Elite Four, the Champion, Victory Road's ten, the route trainers, the mansion guardians). What a cardless player loses is the ambient layer and the association NPC, not the ladder
trainer_card.why: Pallet, because of what the town is rather than because it is first on the road. TOWN_CHARACTER.md's hometown row is 'Pallet Town as it was in Kanto, whole, set down on ground that is not Kanto', with Oak's Lab standing: it is the one town in the region that IS a house, and the place a journey is authorised. A licence handed over at home is the scene the town was placed to reproduce, and PROGRESSION_LADDER.md section 5.1 recommends exactly this ('a hometown handing over the licence is the right scene', open decision Q-4). It must also precede the walk: the stretch from Pallet through Route 1 to Brock is where the ambient layer teaches a player what a trainer is, and a card bought at Brock's leaves that whole stretch empty of them. The alternative, gym1_town, is the masons' and rescue town, and PROGRESSION_LADDER section 1.1 already gives it the workstation upgrades: a mason's yard has no claim on a trainer credential. Inside Pallet there is no second candidate, hometown_mart being the town's only counter.
trainer_card.price_why: 500 is Cobbleverse's own price for this exact item, read from base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/default_shop.json's 'Cards' category (2026-10-01), and the category name here is that file's too. The figure is not ours to invent and there are two reasons to leave it alone. First, it prices the card as a tax on the first hour rather than a purchase: 500 against Mart basics of 200/200/100 is two and a half Poké Balls, paid out of wild-Pokémon income alone (earnCobbleDollarsFromWildPokemon: true at cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier: 0.5), because trainer income is the thing it unlocks. Second, whether CobbleDollars falls back to defaultShop for a merchant carrying no shop compound is NOT VERIFIED (PROGRESSION_LADDER U-3). If it does, the card may already be buyable and this counter is belt and braces -- and at 500 the player meets one price by either route. Any cheaper figure would put two prices on one item. No measurement of CobbleDollars per hour exists (U-1), so re-price with the rest of the ladder when it does, not on its own.
trainer_card.buys_why: rctmod:trainer_card is not in base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/bank.json (checked 2026-10-01), so nothing in the pack buys it back. A licence that can be sold is sold once the trainers start paying.

stones.name: Assayer
stones.status: built as data 2026-09-28 (the owner: build the stone economy); the price is STONE_ECONOMY.md's proposed floor, open decision O-6
stones.why: STONE_ECONOMY.md section 8: the Exchange sells every stone and never buys, because the faces are an unlimited supply and a stone with a sell price would make a face a money printer. It is the catch-up for a player who skipped a place, not the supply. No stone is in CobbleDollars' bank.json, so nothing else buys one back. The shop is authored (tools/traders.py stone_shop), in the offer shape the template itself carries ({Item:{count,id},Price:"<n>"}); that it sells in game is proof P-7, not run
